speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual suggestion for a newborn; the yellowing you describe spreading from the face to the trunk with scleral icterus is classic for jaundice, not appendicitis. Have your parents noticed any poor feeding, excessive sleepiness, or a high-pitched cry in addition to the discoloration?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born full term at 38 weeks via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. No past medical history. Social history: Exclusive breastfeeding every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological Jaundice (Breastfeeding Jaundice)

The history of exclusive breastfeeding every 2–3 hours, combined with the progression of jaundice from the face to the trunk and scleral icterus, is highly consistent with physiological or breastfeeding jaundice. The previous suggestion of appendicitis was incorrect given the clinical presentation; please ensure the infant is feeding frequently to help resolve this condition.
